summary: The note describes the R-class patrol boats, a class of Finnish vessels originally built as coastal minesweepers. They were converted into patrol boats by the end of the 1960s, transferred to the Patrol Flotilla and later the 7th Missile Flotilla, and used for sea patrol and anti-submarine warfare. The class was stricken from the Finnish Navy list in the 1990s. Three later, somewhat larger vessels are sometimes called the Rihtniemi or Ruissalo class, but the Finnish Navy designated all five as R class.
one_line: A class of Finnish coastal minesweepers converted into patrol and anti-submarine boats in the late 1960s, retired in the 1990s.
key_facts: The R-class patrol boats were a class of Finnish patrol boats.
The R-class vessels were originally constructed as coastal minesweepers.
The R-class boats were modified into patrol boats by the end of the 1960s.
After modification, the R-class boats were transferred to the Patrol Flotilla and later to the 7th Missile Flotilla.
The R-class boats were used for sea patrol and as anti-submarine warfare vessels.
The R-class boats were stricken from the Finnish Navy list in the 1990s.
The three later vessels were named "Ruissalo", "Raisio" and "Röyttä".
The three later vessels were somewhat larger than the earlier R-class boats.
The later vessels are sometimes referred to as the Rihtniemi and "Ruissalo" classes.
The Finnish Navy used the designation R class for all five vessels.
